title: Tenant-protective auto-throttle and fallback policy for regional routing
creator: Aisha Patel
body: Problem: We currently have coarse fallback triggers that flip entire regions or tiers into lower-capacity variants after surge events. This causes noisy multi-tenant impact and recovery thrash for high-traffic customers. We need a tenant-protective automatic fallback and throttling policy that: 1) Detects 429 spikes, backend timeouts, and elevated error rates per-route and per-tenant; 2) Computes a composite signal (score) with hysteresis and probation windows; 3) Triggers circuit-breaker actions scoped to tenant + route + region (not global), including soft-throttle, routing to fallback model variants, and temporary request rejection when needed. Goals: - Minimize cross-tenant collateral damage during overloads - Preserve SLOs for priority tiers while shedding load from noisy tenants - Provide fast, observable, and reversible actions with clear cooldowns - Ensure we can safely fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants without data correctness surprises Proposed design: - Signals: 429 rate (windowed), p95 latency, backend timeout count, error-rate (5xx). Each signal is normalized and weighted into a composite trip_score. - Scoring: per-tenant rolling window of 1m, 5m, 15m; trip_score uses decayed max across windows to catch spikes. - Thresholds: trip_score > 0.8 opens tenant circuit; 0.5-0.8 puts tenant into probation/soft-throttle; <0.3 clears. Thresholds configurable per-tier (P0 customers have higher tolerance). - Circuit states: CLOSED (normal), SOFT_OPEN (throttle fraction, route subset to fallback), OPEN (automated routing to fallback and strict token bucket rejection for excess), HALF_OPEN (probation where a small probe fraction goes to primary). - Fallback variants: prefer functional-compatible smaller/quantized variants (e.g., v1.3-q8-k30) with compatibility rules (max prompt length, functions support). Annotate model catalog entries with fallback_compat tags. - Regional dampening: aggregate trip_score across region at route level to decide regional cutover only when > X% of active tenants are tripping to avoid single-tenant region-level actions. - Tenant probation: exponential backoff cooldowns and decay of trip_score; when HALF_OPEN, allow 2% of traffic for 30s probes. - SLO-aware weighting: for tenants with explicit SLOs (enterprise customers), include penalty terms so we avoid false positives. - Observability: wire trip_score, circuit state, per-action events to Console; add prebuilt dashboard and alert rules (critical alerts when >3 enterprise tenants enter OPEN). - Rollout: feature flag gated; canary: enable for 5% of traffic across non-enterprise tenants in us-west-2 for 48h; extend to other regions after metrics look good. - Safety: fail-closed to primary only when model compatibility check fails; fallback action is reversible and logged. - API: expose admin endpoints to view/override circuit state per-tenant and to set emergency cooldowns. Implementation scope: - Orchestrator change to compute trip_score stream and persist circuit state in state-store - Router policy change to consult per-tenant circuit and apply throttling/fallback decisions - Model catalog metadata extension for fallback_compat tags - Console changes for dashboard, alerts, and admin controls - E2E tests using routing-sim-v2 and chaos harness for simulated timeouts and 429 storms
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant trip_score is computed and emitted to telemetry every 10s
Router consults tenant circuit state and applies soft-throttle/fallback for canary traffic
HALF_OPEN probing behavior exercises primary models and returns to CLOSED when stable
Regional aggregation prevents region-wide cutover for single-tenant spikes in simulated tests
Dashboards show circuit state and a generated incident when 3+ enterprise tenants open circuits
Canary rollout completes without violating 99th percentile latency SLO for enterprise tenants
notes: 2025-11-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after post-mortem on 2025-11-03 outage where a single tenant's retry storm caused regional model fallbacks.
2025-11-11 Marco Nguyen: Prototype trip_score function in routing-sim-v2 (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1427). Early sims show reduced collateral for noisy tenants.
2025-11-12 Design review (Anita Rao): request to add explicit model capability checks before fallback to avoid breaking function-calling customers. Added note to model catalog metadata.
2025-11-13 Security review (Jared Lin): recommended that admin override endpoints require workspace-admin role + request audit log entry. Implemented RBAC checks in auth layer.
2025-11-14 Trade-off discussion: aggressive thresholds reduce primary SLO violations but increase fallback churn. Decided on conservative default thresholds and per-tier overrides.
2025-11-15 QA plan: routing-sim-v2 scenarios: steady-state noise, retry storm, regional outage, slow-model degradation. Run with real traffic replay for 24h in staging.
2025-11-16 Marco Nguyen: Implemented backend to persist circuit state in etcd with TTL-based cooldown and exposed admin GET/POST endpoints. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1458
2025-11-17 Ops feedback (Priya Verma): add an Escalation policy: if any enterprise tenant remains OPEN for >10m generate page to #oncall-routing and open an incident ticket. Added to alerts plan.
Next steps: finish router policy integration, add model catalog fallback_compat tagging, write canary runbook, and schedule staged rollout week of 2025-11-24.
